ar_hippie_wall.blurb: Hippie Wall forms the western end of the Cave Creek cliffline, in the Sam's Throne area of north-central Arkansas. It holds seven routes on sandstone, six of them trad and just one bolted line. Grades run from 5.7 to 5.10, and most of the lines sit in the 5.10 range, so it suits climbers who are comfortable placing their own gear. The climbing mixes crack and face moves, and the wall gets a blend of sun and shade through the day. The routes sit between the two walk-down paths that lead to the base of the cliff.

ar_matter_of_time_boulder.blurb: This is one boulder in the Point Boulders cluster at Sam's Throne in north-central Arkansas, holding seven problems on sandstone. Difficulty is wide: one easy problem near V0, a handful of mid-grade lines in the V2 to V6 range, and two of the hardest problems at V8. The boulder gets afternoon sun. The back of it is short and dirty, so the climbing is on the far side. Reaching it means leaving the main trail toward the Throne and Patio boulders and following a faint path that is hard to spot in fall and winter.

ar_the_den.blurb: The Den is a small bouldering spot on top of a ridge near the river, a few minutes outside Norfork in northeast Arkansas. It has seven sandstone problems ranging from V1 to V7, with most in the V3 to V5 range and a single hard line at the top end. The style runs from moderate to steep, and the photos show cave-like terrain and a prow that carries the tallest problems. The walk in from the trailhead is short on a good trail.

ar_space_wall.blurb: Space Wall is part of the Area 51 sector of Bigfoot Hollow, in the eastern Boston Mountains near Ozark, Arkansas. It has seven routes, mostly bolted with one trad line, and it is the place in the hollow where most of the easy climbing is found. Grades start around 5.6 and move up through the 5.9 and 5.10 range to one 5.12 line, so a mixed group can find something. The wall sits further along the cliff band than the MMA wall, a short hike from the roundabout trailhead.

ar_cave_roof.blurb: Cave Roof is a small bouldering sector at Area 74, a sandstone bouldering area in northwest Arkansas roughly an hour from Fayetteville. It has six problems, running from V1 up to V7, with a couple of easy lines, a few in the middle, and two hard ones. The features are two cave roofs with a dihedral between them. It sits on the climber's right of the Main Wall, a short way past where the sidewalk ends.

ar_haw_creek_west_valinor.blurb: Haw Creek West, also called Valinor, is a small cliff in the Big Piney region of north-central Arkansas, near the falls and campground at Haw Creek. It has six routes: four sport and two trad. Grades span from 5.8 to the low 5.11 range, with most of the lines around 5.10. The wall offers both sun and shade, and the short hike to it can be hard to follow, though the walking itself is easy.

ar_road_warrior_area.blurb: Road Warrior Area is a small section of Lake Lincoln, west of Fayetteville in northwest Arkansas. It has just a handful of routes: six in all, four bolted and two trad. Grades run from 5.6 to 5.11, with the middle of the range in the 5.9 and 5.10 grades, so beginners and intermediate climbers both have options. It lies along the cliff from the Mad Max area, a minute or two of walking from there, away from the main trail between two busier sections.

ar_metal_wall.blurb: Metal Wall is a section of Jamestown Crag, the sandstone sport crag near Batesville in northeast Arkansas. It has six bolted routes, all in the 5.7 to 5.9 range, mostly 5.8, which makes it an easy-grade wall. The rock is broken by large flakes. It lies just around the right-hand corner from the Game Wall. To get there, take the Dog Walk descent and turn left at the bottom.
